references.text: The parallel passage in Deuteronomy repeats the command to honor father and mother, with the addition that it will go well with you.
Leviticus repeats the commandment to fear mother and father, linked to the laws of holiness.
Proverbs urges listening to a father's instruction and not rejecting a mother's guidance.
Proverbs warns against despising a father's commands or a mother's teaching.
Proverbs reminds us to listen to our father and not despise our mother in her old age.
It states the serious consequences for anyone who curses their father or mother.
A curse upon anyone who shows contempt for their father or mother.
Ezekiel mentions dishonoring of father and mother among Jerusalem's sins.
Malachi uses the relationship between son and father as a picture of reverence.
Jesus quotes the commandment and criticizes the Pharisees for circumventing it through traditions.
Jesus mentions the command to honor father and mother in his conversation with the rich young man.
Mark recounts Jesus' criticism of traditions that nullify the command to honor parents.
Jesus quotes the commandment in his conversation with the rich man.
Luke records Jesus' reference to the commandment in his conversation with the rich ruler.
Paul quotes the commandment directly and emphasizes the promise of long life attached to it.
Paul urges children to obey their parents in everything, for this is pleasing to the Lord.
Highlights that 'living long' fundamentally depends on loving and obeying God, where honoring parents is a central part of this obedience.
Confirms the general theological principle that obedience to God's way brings long life in the land, where honoring parents is part of this way.
